name: ICANotes vs Valant
title: ICANotes vs Valant: Psychiatry EHR Comparison (2026)
description: Compare ICANotes and Valant for psychiatric practices. See differences in documentation speed, e-prescribing, outcome tracking, pricing, and which EHR is best for your psychiatry practice.

summary.bottom_line: ICANotes excels at rapid documentation with its unique 75,000+ phrase library and menu-driven templates—ideal for psychiatrists who need to document complex medication visits quickly. Valant is better for larger organizations that prioritize standardized data capture, outcome analytics, and team-based workflows.

key_differences.documentation_approach: ICANotes (menu-driven phrase library) vs Valant (checklist-style templates)

sections.heading: ICANotes vs Valant: Overview
sections.content: ICANotes and Valant are both leading EHR platforms for behavioral health, but they take fundamentally different approaches to clinical documentation. ICANotes was designed by a practicing psychiatrist and is the only EHR in the market with a 75,000+ phrase content library for rapid note assembly. Valant emphasizes standardized data capture and robust outcome analytics, making it popular with larger organizations focused on tracking treatment effectiveness.

sections.heading: Documentation Approach
sections.content: This is the key differentiator. ICANotes uses a unique menu-driven system where clinicians click to select pre-written clinical phrases that auto-generate narrative, audit-ready notes. This approach is particularly valuable for psychiatrists documenting complex medication management visits—users report significantly faster documentation times compared to free-text entry. Valant takes a checklist-style approach with standardized fields designed for consistent data capture. Many groups find ICANotes faster for narrative-heavy encounters, while Valant suits teams prioritizing standardized fields and analytics.

sections.heading: e-Prescribing & Medication Management
sections.content: Both platforms offer integrated e-prescribing with EPCS support for controlled substances. Valant has a slight edge with built-in PDMP lookups directly in the prescribing workflow. ICANotes also supports e-prescribing and has over 100 built-in rating scales (PHQ-9, GAD-7, etc.) that integrate seamlessly with medication monitoring documentation.

sections.heading: Outcome Tracking & Analytics
sections.content: Valant is the stronger choice for organizations that prioritize outcome measurement and analytics. It offers robust reporting dashboards, configurable clinical workflows, and tools for tracking patient progress over time. This is particularly valuable for practices participating in value-based care or needing to demonstrate treatment effectiveness. ICANotes offers basic outcome tracking but doesn't match Valant's analytics depth.

sections.heading: Which Should You Choose?
sections.content: The choice depends on what you prioritize most in your daily workflow:

recommendations.when: Documentation speed is your top priority, you're documenting complex psychiatric evaluations, you want transparent pricing, or you're a solo/small practice psychiatrist who values the phrase library approach

You need robust outcome analytics and reporting, you're running a larger behavioral health organization, you prioritize standardized data capture for team-based care, or you're participating in value-based care arrangements
Both have solid e-prescribing and EPCS—the documentation style and analytics needs should drive your decision

faqs.q: Which is faster for psychiatric documentation: ICANotes or Valant?
faqs.a: ICANotes is generally faster for documentation due to its unique menu-driven phrase library. Psychiatrists can build detailed, narrative notes by clicking to select pre-written clinical phrases rather than typing from scratch. Valant's checklist approach is efficient but typically requires more manual entry for complex narrative documentation.

faqs.q: Is ICANotes or Valant better for group practices?
faqs.a: For larger group practices focused on standardized workflows and outcome tracking, Valant is typically the better choice. Its analytics dashboards and consistent data capture are valuable for team-based care. For smaller psychiatry groups prioritizing documentation speed, ICANotes may be more practical.

faqs.q: Do both ICANotes and Valant support controlled substance prescribing?
faqs.a: Yes, both platforms support EPCS (Electronic Prescribing of Controlled Substances). Valant has integrated PDMP lookups in the prescribing workflow. ICANotes also supports e-prescribing including controlled substances with appropriate identity proofing.

faqs.q: Which has more transparent pricing: ICANotes or Valant?
faqs.a: ICANotes has more transparent pricing, ranging from $35 to $213 per month depending on features and practice size. Valant uses custom enterprise pricing that requires contacting sales for a quote, making it harder to compare costs upfront.
